LIBS can be used to: (1) rapidly and accurately identify bacteria; (2) rapidly and accurately detect and quantify the presence of bacteria and other biological contaminants; (3) rapidly and accurately quantify the concentrations of a wide variety of chemical compounds in a biological sample; (4) accurately detect and identify the presence of various biological materials in a sample; (5) accurately detect and quantify various biomolecules; and (6) rapidly and accurately analyse the chemical composition of biological tissues.

the LIBS technology has evolved into a powerful, nondestructive, real-time, reagentless analytical technique for the rapid, accurate and sensitive detection, biochemical characterization and identification of various biological, biomedical and clinical samples.

LIBS can rapidly detect and accurately identify various types of biological samples, and can be used to biochemically analyze biological specimens in a reagentless manner, with high sensitivity and specificity, and in a real-time fashion.

the application of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopic techniques to the rapid analysis of biological materials and the development of a new class of laser-based medical devices for use in the detection and diagnosis of diseases.

the future of LIBS in the field of medicine is very promising.

LIBS is an ideal technique for rapid, in situ, and real-time analysis and identification of biological and biomedical samples.

the biomedical applications of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopies (LIBS) have the potential to be a significant advancement in the diagnosis and treatment of disease, and in the monitoring of the efficacy of medical therapies.
